author: amazon-q-developer
body:
:stop_sign: **Security Vulnerability**: The `-sf` flags cause curl to fail silently when API errors occur, resulting in empty or invalid tokens being used. This can cause authentication failures without clear error messages. Replace `-sf` with `-fS` to fail loudly and display errors.[^1]
```suggestion
INSTALLATION_TOKEN=$(curl -fS -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $JWT" \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
  "" | jq -r '.token')
```

[^1]: CWE-391: Unchecked Error Condition - https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/391.html

source_pr_title: Add gha-runner chart for self-hosted GitHub Actions runners
author: amazon-q-developer
body:
:stop_sign: **Logic Error**: The JWT generation lacks validation that required environment variables are set. If GITHUB_APP_ID is missing or empty, the JWT will be malformed. Add validation at the start of the script to prevent silent failures.[^1]
```suggestion
# Generate GitHub App JWT
if [ -z "$GITHUB_APP_ID" ] || [ -z "$GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID" ] || [ -z "$GITHUB_OWNER" ]; then
  echo "Error: Required environment variables are not set"
  exit 1
fi

NOW=$(date +%s)
EXP=$((NOW + 600))
HEADER='{"alg":"RS256","typ":"JWT"}'
PAYLOAD='{"iat":"'$NOW'","exp":"'$EXP'","iss":"'$GITHUB_APP_ID'"}'
```

[^1]: CWE-754: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions - https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html

<sub>:red_circle: HIGH RISK</sub>

Using a static `RUNNER_NAME` prevents scaling the deployment beyond 1 replica because GitHub requires unique names for runners in a pool. Consider using the Kubernetes Downward API to provide the Pod name as the runner name when a custom name isn't provided.

Try running the following prompt in your coding agent:
> Modify the `containerEnv` in `packages/charts/gha-runner/src/construct.ts` to use `metadata.name` via the Downward API for `RUNNER_NAME` when `props.runnerName` is not specified.
